A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Parkinson’s disease is characterized by an apparent iron dysregulation, in which iron is accumulated in some regions (dorsal substantia nigra), but decreased in others (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex).
iron dysregulation is not limited to specific regions in the brain, but rather it is distributed in a whole-brain pattern.
the pattern of iron accumulation in the basal ganglia, neocortex and cerebellum in Parkinson’s disease is far more extensive and complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the whole-brain pattern in Parkinson’s disease is far more complex than previously thought, with a combination of increased and decreased iron levels in the brain.
quantitative susceptibility mapping is an effective method to assess the whole-brain distribution of iron in patients with Parkinson’s disease.
the brain-wide distribution of magnetic susceptibility alterations is not only a powerful biomarker of Parkinson’s disease but also an informative marker of iron dysregulations in the brain.
